The problem in corank $0$ can be viewed as the search for a real analog of Murthy's celebrating splitting theorem in the algebraically closed case: to wit, beyond the vanishing of the top Chern class in Chow theory, are the obstructions to splitting ``purely topological''? In a sense, the answer in this case is yes, and we give a proof, using motivic techniques, of a mild extension of the results of Bhatwadekar-Sridharan and Bhatwadekar-Das-Mandal. In corank $1$, in the algebraically closed situation, Murthy's splitting conjecture (now a theorem in characteristic $0$) predicts that the vanishing of the top Chern class in Chow theory is the only obstruction to splitting off a free rank $1$ summand, and we can search for a suitable ``real'' analog of this assertion. We observe that several natural guesses for a ``real'' analog of Murthy's splitting conjecture cannot be true, i.e., that the situation over the real numbers is rather complicated.
item.dc:creator: Aravind Asok, Jean Fasel, Samuel Lerbet

item.title: Equivariant Koszul Cohomology of Canonical Curves
item.description: arXiv:2512.19894v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates the representation-theoretic structure of the Koszul cohomology of a smooth projective variety $X$ over an algebraically closed field $k$, admitting an action of a finite group $G$ of order coprime to ${\rm char}(k)$. Properties of $G$-equivariant functors are employed to show that the associated Koszul complex is a complex of $kG$-modules, and to generalize known dimension formulas to identities between virtual representations. In the case of canonical curves, explicit formulas are obtained by combining the theory of equivariant Euler characteristics and equivariant Riemann-Roch theorems with that of generating functions for Schur functors.
item.dc:creator: Kostas Karagiannis, Aristides Kontogeorgis, Konstantia Manousou Sotiropoulou

item.title: Jacobian rings and the infinitesimal Torelli Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2601.17765v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article we deal with jacobian rings and identify a mixed Hodge component of a nondegenerate hypersurface in the torus with a lattice geometric quotient vector space. We introduce a period map, study its differential and compute the kernel of the differential much explicitly via certain Laurent polynomials. As a main application we deal with the infinitesimal Torelli theorem (ITT). We study the kernel of the cohomological map for explicit deformations and complete our study by dealing with the remaining part $\coker(\kappa_{\mathbb{P},f})$ (cokernel of the Kodaira-Spencer map) in dimensions $n \geq 4$.
item.dc:creator: Julius Giesler

item.title: Categorical resolutions and birational geometry of nodal Gushel-Mukai varieties
item.description: arXiv:2602.14109v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study ordinary Gushel--Mukai varieties with one node in dimensions three, four, and five, under some generality hypotheses. The blowup of the node is related by a relative Atiyah flop to a quadric fibration over $\PP^2$. We identify the categorical resolution of the Kuznetsov component with the Clifford component of this fibration. Then, we study hyperbolic equivalence, the relation with Verra varieties, and birational Torelli for general nodal threefolds. For fourfolds, we prove that a countable union of divisorial families is dense in the complex topology, with rational members and untwisted degree-two $K3$ categories. Finally, we construct a spinor modification of the associated conic bundle and compute its trace-free endomorphism bundle, which is not a sum of line bundles.
item.dc:creator: Kacper Grzelakowski, Marco Rampazzo, Shizhuo Zhang

item.title: Rational chain connectedness in the complex analytic setting
item.description: arXiv:2602.19415v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend Hacon--M\textsuperscript{c}Kernan's rational chain connectedness theorem to the complex analytic setting. As a consequence, we prove that the fibers of any resolution of singularities of complex analytic kawamata log terminal singularities are rationally chain connected. In contrast to the original approach, we avoid the use of extension theorems and instead rely on the minimal model program.
item.dc:creator: Osamu Fujino

item.title: Genus $2$ pencils on surfaces with $p_g=K^2=1$, envelopes, and conics tangent to plane cubic curves
item.description: arXiv:2603.03132v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider $(1,1)$-surfaces, namely, minimal compact complex surfaces $S$ with $p_g (S) =K_S^2=1$: for these the bicanonical map is a covering of degree $4$ of the plane $P^2$. And we answer a question posed by Meng Chen, whether they can contain a genus 2 pencil (this is the standard reason of failure of birationality of the bicanonical map). Our main theorem says that those which admit a genus 2 pencil form an irreducible subvariety of codimension $3$ in their moduli space $\frak M_{[1,1]}$; moreover, the general such surface admits exactly $24$ such pencils, corresponding to $12$ pencils of conics in $P^2$. The real fun is to relate this variety to the geometry of pencils of conics in the plane everywhere tangent to a cubic curve and a line. We investigate the corresponding variety $\cal{T}$ of triples and provide explicit equations using the classical theory of envelopes: among others, equations given in terms of the Weierstrass normal form of the cubic.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Catanese (Accademia dei Lincei), Noah Ruhland (Universit\"at Bayreuth)

item.title: Deligne's weight spectral sequence and tautological cohomology of the moduli space of curves
item.description: arXiv:2603.26962v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We have written a computer program that implements Deligne's pullback and pushforward weight spectral sequences to compute the weight graded pieces of the rational cohomology of moduli spaces of pointed smooth curves (as well as curves of compact type and curves with rational tails) in cases where the cohomology groups appearing in the boundary stratification of the Deligne-Mumford compactification are generated by tautological classes (and when Pixton's relations are all relations). The weight graded pieces are computed together with the induced action of the symmetric group permuting the points on the curves. Using the computer program we have determined this information in the case of genus five as well as in the case of genus three with three marked points.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Bergstr\"om, Thomas Wennink

item.title: Hyper-Operations and Coherent Plasmas over $\mathbb{F}_1$
item.description: arXiv:2604.24568v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The additive structure of $\mathbb{F}_1$-modules (in the sense of Segal's $\Gamma$-sets) differs fundamentally from that of abelian groups: addition is encoded through a family of $n$-ary hyper-operations that are multivalued and need not satisfy classical associativity. We establish a \emph{law of generalized associativity} showing that, despite this failure of strict associativity, every $n$-ary sum is contained in the iterated hypersum associated with any partition of its inputs. This enables us to give a hyper-additive description on $\pi_0$ of Schwede's linearization functor $-\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_1} \mathbb{Z}: \mathbb{F}_1\mathbf{Mod} \to \mathbf{Ab}$ that universally strictifies the hyper-additive structure of $\mathbb{F}_1$-modules into classical abelian group addition. We then introduce coherent plasmas, whose algebraic structure encodes the coherence condition inherent in $\mathbb{F}_1$-modules. We construct fully faithful nerves for these structures and their finite-arity truncations, yielding a compatible tower of adjunctions, as well as a coherent Segal condition that characterizes the essential image. The levels of these nerves are represented by powerset plasmas $P_n$, which arise as algebraic realizations of representable $\Gamma$-sets, analogous to standard simplices in geometric realization.
item.dc:creator: Luqiao Xu

item.title: \'Etale Fundamental Groups: a geometric and topological approach to fundamental groups in algebraic geometry
item.description: arXiv:2606.23906v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This thesis explores the notion of fundamental groups across three mathematical settings. We begin with the classical topological theory of covering spaces, highlighting its structural analogy with Galois theory. We then follow Grothendieck in transporting these ideas to algebraic geometry. The inadequacy of the Zariski topology motivates the \'etale topology, from which the \'etale fundamental group is constructed and compared to its topological counterpart via transcendental methods. Finally, we linearise the theory through Tannakian duality, where fundamental groups are recovered as automorphism groups of fibre functors on certain monoidal categories, a framework broad enough to encompass \'etale, topological, and motivic Galois groups alike.
item.dc:creator: Loris De Vos

item.title: On arrangements of plane real quartics with respect to three lines
item.description: arXiv:2607.19457v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We complete the classification of mutual arrangements of a smooth real algebraic or real pseudoholomorphic quartic curve and three lines under condition that each oval of the quartic intersects the union of the lines. This classification was started in a recent preprint by Maletto. There is one arrangement which is realizable pseudoholomorphically but not algebraically. It can be constructed in different ways, in particular, by a combinatorial patchworking on an irregular triangulation. This is the first example of a combinatorial patchworking which produces a PL curve in $RP^2$ whose arrangement relative to the coordinate axes is algebraically unrealizable.
item.dc:creator: S. Yu. Orevkov

item.title: Quantum index, Arnold-Rokhlin surfaces, and real enumerative geometry
item.description: arXiv:2607.21251v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The main goal of this note is to relate two different Welschinger-type rules of signs that were used for definition of real enumerative invariants of toric surfaces (the invariants considered being relative to the toric boundary). The relation between them intertwines Mikhalkin's quantum index and geometry of real and complex point sets of counted real curves. As a by-product, we suggest a new definition of quantum index, which can be used for refined invariant enumeration of real algebraic curves on surfaces in a non-toric setup.
item.dc:creator: Ilia Itenberg, Eugenii Shustin

item.title: Instanton slices and their superpolynomials
item.description: arXiv:2607.25666v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The key theorem is a connection between motivic superpolynomials of plane curve singularities in any ranks with superpolynomials of the corresponding instanton slices, Nekrasov-type instanton sums with conductors. In this case, instanton slices are related to Compactified Jacobians, but they form a much wider class and, generally, have no connection to plane curve singularities. Thus, we extend significantly theory of affine Springer fibers in type A. For instance, we obtain a motivic interpretation (counting $\mathbb{F}_q$-points of some stacks) of superpolynomials for hyperbolic knots K12n242, K12n725, among many others. New formulas for Nekrasov's instanton sums as limits of superpolynomials of families of plane curve singularities are another application, with an impressive connection to nonsymmetric Macdonald polynomials. The main conjecture states that instanton superpolynomials for arbitrary Young diagrams coincide with the corresponding (new) DAHA superpolynomials if and only if the latter are positive or (equivalently) the former are superdual. Only very few such diagrams come from plane curve singularities. Our DAHA superpolynomials are parallel to the EHA ones, but we used the nonsymmetric approach. The connection with Khovanov-Rozansky polynomials of the corresponding Coxeter knots is expected. Among applications: the Volume Conjecture reformulated in terms of instanton slices, topological invariance of unibranch motivic superpolynomials for semigroups with up to 4 generators, a mixed-characteristic conjecture, upgraded Weak Riemann Hypothesis, and superpolynomials for Gorenstein curve singularities and multibranch ones.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Cherednik

item.title: Cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-homology of wonderful models of subspace arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2607.29097v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-homology of De Concini--Procesi wonderful models of subspace arrangements. For a building set $\mathcal{G}$ over a field $k$, we identify the cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-chain complex of $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{G})$ with an $\eta$-twisted nested-set complex carrying Milnor--Witt coefficients and derived orientation data. The key geometric input is a motivic blow-up calculation: for a blow-up along a smooth center of codimension $c$, the relevant connecting class is $(c-1)_\epsilon\eta$, hence it is zero for $c$ odd and $\eta$ for $c$ even. This replaces the parity condition in the computation of Rains by a Milnor--Witt attaching class. As a consequence, the part of cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-homology surviving after multiplication by $\eta$, and also the homology after inverting $\eta$, are expressed by the interval cohomology of the $2$-divisible subposet of the lattice generated by $\mathcal{G}$. For the braid arrangement, the condition becomes the odd-block condition on partitions, yielding explicit decompositions for the cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-homology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,N}$ and examples in low rank.
item.dc:creator: Haoyang Liu, Keyao Peng

item.title: Twisted Deligne modules and abelian varieties over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2608.16668v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Isogeny classes of abelian varieties over finite fields were described by Tate and Honda. Deligne proved that the category of ordinary abelian varieties over a finite field is equivalent to the category of ordinary Deligne modules. Centeleghe and Stix extended Deligne's results to the whole category of abelian varieties, but, if the base finite field is not prime, then the target category is not related to Deligne modules. In this paper we introduce generalized and twisted Deligne modules and give a more direct generalization of the Deligne theorem.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Rybakov

item.title: A L\^e number addendum to the Morse Splitting Lemma
item.description: arXiv:2608.21980v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate how the complex analytic Morse Splitting Lemma relates to the generic L\^e numbers of a function, and what the relation tells us about the function. As special cases, we consider functions for which the 0-dimensional generic L\^e number is at most 3 and functions for which the critical locus has dimension 1.
item.dc:creator: David B. Massey

item.title: Birational cubic fourfolds via an Enriques Cremona transformation
item.description: arXiv:2609.10353v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe a Cremona transformation on $\mathbb{P}^5$ given by the linear system of quintics that are double along the Fano model of an Enriques surface $S$. Using this Cremona transform, we construct a birational equivalence between the very general cubic fourfold $X$ of discriminant 44 and its unique Fourier--Mukai partner. We also classify birational maps between smooth, non-isomorphic cubic fourfolds resolved by blowing up a smooth surface on each side: the centres must be either Fano models of Enriques surfaces, as in our construction, or Veronese surfaces, as studied by Fan--Lai.
item.dc:creator: Corey Brooke, Lisa Marquand

item.title: The Chern character of a coherent sheaf on a smooth projective hypersurface
item.description: arXiv:2609.12759v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a coherent sheaf on a smooth projective hypersurface X, we prove an explicit formula for its Chern character as a Cech cocycle in terms of the free resolution of the associated module and calculate its image in the Jacobian ring under the Griffiths residue map. The formula is a geometric analogue of the Kapustin-Li formula for Landau-Ginzburg models, but proven directly using Hodge-theoretic techniques. This yields an effective method to compute the primitive part of the Chern character of any coherent sheaf using commutative algebra. We finish by proving the Hodge conjecture for the degree 33 Fermat fourfold.
item.dc:creator: David Favero, Tyler L. Kelly

item.title: Chow Vanishing and Motives of Cluster Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2609.19744v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the integral Chow groups $CH_i$ and mixed Hodge degree $H^{2i, (i, i)}$ cohomology groups of a really full rank (RFR) sink-recurrent cluster variety vanish for $i > 0$. In particular this applies to braid varieties and open projected Richardson varieties in any Lie type. Our main technical tool is the construction of a stratification of any RFR sink-recurrent cluster variety $\mathcal{A}(\Sigma)$ over any field $k$ into (affine space times) RFR sink-recurrent cluster varieties of seeds with fewer mutable vertices than $\Sigma$, with which we show that RFR sink-recurrent cluster varieties are linear in the sense of Totaro. We also show that cycle class maps are isomorphisms onto the lowest-weight part of rational Borel-Moore homology for any mixed Tate variety over a number field. Finally, we use our results to deduce vanishing theorems for the Khovanov-Rozansky homology groups of closures of positive braids and generation properties for the Chow groups of flag Richardson, projected Richardson, and brick varieties: namely, that these groups are generated integrally by the fundamental classes of their closed Richardson, positroid, and braid strata, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Josephine Hlavinka

item.title: Bounds for Codimension-One Components of Zero Loci of Bernstein-Sato Ideals
item.description: arXiv:2609.19869v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth complex affine variety of dimension $n$, and let $F=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ be a tuple of nonzero regular functions on $X$ such that $f:=\prod_{i=1}^r f_i$ is not invertible. We study the zero loci of the Bernstein-Sato ideals $B_F^{\mathbf a}$ for nonnegative integral shifts $\mathbf a$. For a fixed log resolution, every codimension-one irreducible component of $Z(B_F^{\mathbf a})$ is a hyperplane of the form $L_E(\mathbf s)+k_E+c=0$ with $c$ a positive integer. We give a new proof of this result using localized maximal and minimal extensions of relative D-modules. We also prove that $c\leq L_E(\mathbf a)+(n-1-\delta_f)L_E(\mathbf 1)-k_E$, where $\delta_f=\min\{n-1,\alpha_f\}$ and $\alpha_f$ is the minimal exponent of $f$. The problem of obtaining such an upper bound for arbitrary tuples (in particular, for $r>1$) was raised by Budur, van der Veer, and Van Werde, and the above inequality resolves it. To obtain the upper bound, we compare the diagonal slice of $Z(B_F^{\mathbf 1})$ with the root set of $b_f$. A finite covering by translates, combined with diagonal specialization and the log-resolution description, shows that these sets have the same least and greatest points. Saito's root estimate at their common least point then yields the upper bound. We further establish a divisor-valued formulation of the local index comparison, recovering the detection of monodromy support via monodromy zeta functions and the multivariable A'Campo formula.
item.dc:creator: Wenzong Guo, Fanghan Xiang

item.title: Searching Schemes With $p$-Adic Neumann Boundary Value Problems
item.description: arXiv:2609.27751v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Firstly, for branched covering maps $f\colon Y\to X$ between smooth, separated schemes of finite type over the integral ring $O_K$ of a non-archimedean local field $K$, the ramification divisor is found to coincide with the divisor of the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the Radon measure associated with an algebraic differential form on $Y$ against the pullback measure of one on $X$, both taking Borel sets of the space $Y(O_K)$ of $O_K$-rational points of $Y$ as input values. Secondly, the ultracontractivity of semigroups generated by Laplacian integral operators having a geodetic-distance-power kernel function is proven, using heat kernel estimates for ultrametric operators on $p$-adic balls. Thirdly, a series of $p$-adic Neumann Boundary Value Problems, depending on algebraic and pluricanonical differential forms with poles on spaces $X(O_K)$ coming from schemes is formulated and solved, extending previous work of the author. These results are then used to solve reconstruction problems on schemes: the divisor of a pluricanonical form with poles with at worst log-terminal singularities, as well as Weierstrass points of projective algebraic curves can be reconstructed via repeatedly finding weak solutions of $p$-adic Neumann Boundary Value Problems.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Erik Bradley

item.title: An elliptic Calabi-Yau threefold of Mordell-Weil rank twelve
item.description: arXiv:2610.01276v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a smooth projective Calabi-Yau threefold with a flat elliptic fibration of Mordell-Weil rank twelve and Hodge numbers $(h^{1,1},h^{2,1})=(25,1)$. The construction starts from the Kummer surfaces associated with the products of a fixed elliptic curve and the level-four modular family. The threefold is birational to an anticanonical quartic in $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(3)^{\oplus2}\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(4)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1})$. We give twelve independent sections and construct a projective crepant resolution of the associated Weierstrass model. Varying the fixed elliptic curve gives a family of quartic resolutions that is locally complete at the original member. The resulting fourfold is birational over $\mathbb{C}$ to a diagonal order-four quotient of a product of four elliptic curves with $j$-invariant $1728$, and every smooth projective model has Kodaira dimension zero. An algebraic correspondence identifies the third cohomology of the original quartic resolution with the tensor product of the first cohomology of the fixed elliptic curve and the transcendental cohomology of the modular K3 surface. The Galois representation on the latter factor is associated with a weight-three CM newform.
item.dc:creator: Dominik Burek

item.title: Core Coordinates and Negative Support in A-Hypergeometric Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.04369v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a homogeneous $A$-hypergeometric system, let $K_v$ be the intersection of the negative support family for a fake exponent $v$, and let $C_w$ be the set of indices of variables that do not occur in any minimal monomial generator of $\operatorname{in}_w(I_A)$. We prove that $K_v=\operatorname{nsupp}(v)\cap C_w$ holds for every parameter and every fake exponent if and only if $\operatorname{Cone}(A_{C_w})$ meets the interior of $\operatorname{Cone}(A)$. We give equivalent criteria using the reduced Gr\"obner basis and the associated regular triangulation. When the condition fails, we construct an infinite family of fake exponents for which the equality fails.
item.dc:creator: Mao Nagamine

item.title: Local Constancy of the Betti Automorphic Category over the Moduli of Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.12384v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nadler and Yun conjectured that the automorphic side of the Betti geometric Langlands correspondence forms a local system of categories over the moduli of curves. We prove this local constancy conjecture using purely microlocal methods, independent of the recently established Betti geometric Langlands conjecture. In particular, it follows that the Betti automorphic category depends only on the genus of the curve, verifying a conjecture of Ben-Zvi and Nadler.
item.dc:creator: Joakim F{\ae}rgeman, Marius Kj{\ae}rsgaard

item.title: Chow groups of symmetric products of projective spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.20239v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\operatorname{SP}^{d}(\mathbb{P}^{n})$ denote the $d$-th symmetric product of complex projective space.We prove that its integral cycle class map is split injective and has finite cokernel annihilated by $d!$.We also compute the ranks of its Chow groups.By constructing compatible integral retractions on Chow groups and singular homology, we prove that addition of a fixed point induces an isomorphism on the Chow group of $q$-dimensional cycles whenever $d\geq q$.For $n\geq 3$ and $d\geq 6$, we construct a nonalgebraic class of order two in codimension two.Its image generates a direct summand of the cycle class cokernel and remains nonalgebraic after addition of fixed points.Consequently, integral surjectivity fails both at certain finite stages with $q\leq d$ and in the infinite symmetric product.We further identify the codimension two cokernel with third unramified cohomology of the smooth configuration space.Finally, we provide an example where multiplication by an even integer annihilates a nonzero Chow class of order two.
item.dc:creator: Youming Chen, Wenchuan Hu

item.title: Positivity of Wahl defects and specialization of reflexive powers of the canonical sheaf
item.description: arXiv:2610.21092v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(X,E) \to (V,0)$ be the minimal good resolution of a normal complex surface singularity, with $E$ reduced. The Wahl defect is $\Delta(V,0) :=h^1(\mathcal{O}_X)-h^1(S_X)+h^1(\bigwedge^2 S_X)$, where $S_X=\Theta_X(-\log E)$. For non-Gorenstein $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein singularities $(V,0)$, we prove that $\Delta(V,0)\geq0$, with equality precisely in the quasi-homogeneous case. This proves Wahl's Main Conjecture in this class and his $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein and Rational Conjectures. The proof expresses $\Delta$ as the multiplicity of the canonical character in a representation constructed from differential forms and residues. We also prove $\Delta+4p_g\geq0$ for arbitrary normal surface singularities, with equality precisely for rational quasi-homogeneous singularities. For smoothings of rational surface singularities, we give a Riemann--Roch formula for the lengths of the cokernels of the restriction maps to the central fiber for all reflexive canonical powers, in terms of the Milnor number and periodic local Riemann--Roch corrections. This yields numerical and representation-theoretic criteria for $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein smoothings, defined as quotients of equivariant smoothings of the index-one cover with trivial group action on the base. If a rational singularity admits a $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein smoothing, such smoothings are precisely those with minimal Milnor number, or equivalently those whose smoothing components have minimal dimension. Combining these results, we prove that every rational homology disk smoothing is $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein, has a rational weighted homogeneous central fiber, and occurs over a one-dimensional smoothing component. Together with the known weighted homogeneous classification, this completes the analytic classification of normal surface singularities admitting rational homology disk smoothings.
item.dc:creator: Heesang Park, Dongsoo Shin

item.title: Nonlinear neighborhoods of smooth curves and arbitrarily negative Wahl defects
item.description: arXiv:2610.21093v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a theory of nonlinear neighborhoods of smooth projective curves of genus at least two, constructed by gluing products of open subsets of a curve with a disc using nonlinear changes of the disc coordinate. Their zero sections have normal bundles of negative degree and contract to normal surface singularities. For the minimal good resolution $(X,E) \to (V,0)$ of a normal complex surface singularity other than a rational double point, the Wahl defect is defined by $\Delta(V,0) := h^1(\mathcal{O}_X)-h^1(S_X)+h^1(\bigwedge^2S_X)$, where $E$ is reduced and $S_X = \Theta_X(-\log E)$. We give a finite formula for this defect in terms of extension obstructions when $E$ is a single smooth curve. For our constructed neighborhoods, the formula involves extensions of functions alone, includes obstructions at every order, and gives a sharp lower bound depending only on the genus. We apply the theory to hyperelliptic curves and smooth plane curves. Both families consist of singularities that are neither $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein nor quasi-homogeneous. The hyperelliptic examples realize every nonpositive integer as a Wahl defect and attain the genus bound in every genus at least two. They disprove Wahl's Main Conjecture, which asserts nonnegativity for non-Gorenstein singularities, with equality precisely in the quasi-homogeneous case.
item.dc:creator: Heesang Park, Dongsoo Shin

item.title: James reduced product schemes and double quasisymmetric functions
item.description: arXiv:2304.11508v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Symmetric function theory is a key ingredient in the Schubert calculus of Grassmannians. Quasisymmetric functions are analogues that are similarly central to algebraic combinatorics, but for which the associated geometry is poorly developed. Baker and Richter (2008) showed that $\operatorname{QSym}$ manifests topologically as the cohomology ring of the loop suspension of infinite projective space or equivalently of its combinatorial homotopy model, the James reduced product $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$. In recent work, we used this viewpoint to develop topologically-motivated bases of $\operatorname{QSym}$ and initiate a Schubert calculus for $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$ in both cohomology and $K$-theory. Here, we study the torus-equivariant cohomology of $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$. We identify a cellular basis and introduce double monomial quasisymmetric functions as combinatorial representatives, analogous to the factorial Schur functions and double Schubert polynomials of classical Schubert calculus. We also provide a combinatorial Littlewood--Richardson-type rule for the structure coefficients of this basis. Furthermore, we introduce an algebro-geometric analogue of the James reduced product construction. In particular, we prove that the James reduced product of a complex (quasi-)projective variety also carries the structure of a (quasi-)projective variety.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Pechenik, Matthew Satriano

item.title: A new look at unitarity in quantization commutes with reduction for toric manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2412.17157v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a symplectic manifold $M$ with the Hamiltonian action of a compact Lie group $G$, we give a new perspective on the problem of unitarity in the quantization commutes with reduction correspondence. We argue that this correspondence leads naturally to the introduction of what we call Fourier polarizations, whose real directions include the Hamiltonian vector fields of all invariant functions of the moment map. For a Fourier polarization, quantization commutes with reduction unitarily. For a general $G$-invariant polarization, $\mathcal{P}$, unitarity in the quantization commutes with reduction correspondence can then be formulated in terms of the existence of a Fourier polarization, $\mathcal{P}_F$, such that the quantizations with respect to $\mathcal{P}$ and to $\mathcal{P}_F$ are unitarily equivalent. We describe this perspective in detail for symplectic toric manifolds, by considering symplectic reductions associated to the action of a subtorus $T^p\subset T^n$. We consider half-form quantization in Fourier (mixed) polarizations $\mathcal{P}_\infty$, whose real directions are generated by(the Hamiltonian vector fields of the)components of the $T^p$ moment map. We show that Fourier mixed polarizations of this type can be obtained by Mabuchi geodesic rays of toric K\"ahler structures, starting at a given initial structure and with velocity given by the norm square of the moment map of the torus subgroup. We lift these geodesic rays to the quantum bundle via generalized coherent state transforms, which define equivariant isomorphisms between quantum Hilbert spaces for the K\"ahler and Fourier polarizations, where the later are obtained at infinite geodesic time. Unitarity in quantization commutes with reduction in these cases then becomes equivalent to the unitarity of these isomorphisms. In general, however, in the toric case, these isomorphisms are not unitary.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e M. Mour\~ao, Jo\~ao P. Nunes, Augusto Pereira, Dan Wang

item.title: On a specialization of Toda eigenfunctions
item.description: arXiv:2502.10655v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper studies rational functions $\mathfrak{J}_\alpha(q)$, which depend on a positive element $\alpha$ of the root lattice of a root system. These functions arise as Shapovalov pairings of Whittaker vectors in Verma modules of highest weight $-\rho$ for quantum groups and as Hilbert series of Zastava spaces, and are related to the Toda system. They are specializations of multivariate functions more commonly studied in the literature. We investigate the denominator of these rational functions and give an explicit combinatorial formula for the numerator in type A. We also propose a conjectural realization of the numerator as the Poincar\'e polynomial of a smooth variety in type A.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Labelle

item.title: On certain Lagrangian subvarieties in minimal resolutions of Kleinian singularities
item.description: arXiv:2504.08717v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Kleinian singularities are quotients of $\mathbb{C}^2$ by finite subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$. They are in bijection with the simply-laced Dynkin diagrams via the McKay correspondence. Anti-Poisson involutions and their fixed point loci appear naturally in the classification of irreducible Harish-Chandra modules over Kleinian singularities. There are three goals of this paper. The first is to classify anti-Poisson involutions of Kleinian singularities up to conjugation by graded Poisson automorphisms. The second is to describe the scheme-theoretic fixed point loci of Kleinian singularities under anti-Poisson involutions. The third and main goal is to describe the scheme-theoretic preimages of the fixed point loci under minimal resolutions of Kleinian singularities. These preimages are singular Lagrangian subvarieties in the minimal resolutions whose irreducible components are $\mathbb{P}^1$'s and $\mathbb{A}^1$'s. Additionally, we discuss the connections between anti-Poisson involutions and Lie algebra involutions.
item.dc:creator: Mengwei Hu

item.title: On maximal curves of $n$-correct sets
item.description: arXiv:2507.11207v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Suppose $\mathcal{X}$ is an $n$-correct set of nodes in the plane, that is, it admits a unisolvent interpolation with bivariate polynomials of total degree less than or equal to $n.$ Then an algebraic curve $q$ of degree $k\le n$ can pass through at most $d(n,k):={{n+2}\choose {2}}-{{n+2-k}\choose {2}}$ nodes of $\mathcal{X}$. A curve $q$ of degree $k\le n$ is called maximal if it passes through exactly $d(n,k)$ nodes of $\mathcal{X}$. In particular, a maximal line is a line passing through $d(n,1)=n+1$ nodes of $\mathcal{X}$. Maximal curves are an important tool for the study of $n$-correct sets. We present new properties of maximal curves, as well as extensions of known properties.
item.dc:creator: H. Hakopian, G. Vardanyan, N. Vardanyan

item.title: Envelope of Holomorphy of Matsuki Orbits in Complex Grassmannians
item.description: arXiv:2509.17001v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the envelopes of holomorphy of Matsuki orbits $M_{\ell,m,r}$ arising as intersections of $G_0$- and $K$-orbits in complex Grassmannians. These orbits, equipped with natural CR-structures, form a class of compact homogeneous CR-submanifolds whose analytic continuation properties are of fundamental interest. Building on Rossi's theory of holomorphic extension, we establish that the envelope of holomorphy of each Matsuki orbit coincides biholomorphically with the containing $K$-orbit $O_{\ell,m}$. Our approach provides a geometric proof based on the holomorphic fiber bundle structure $\pi : M_{\ell,m,r} \to \mathrm{Gr}_{\ell}(E_+) \times \mathrm{Gr}_{m}(E_-)$, clarifying the role of compact isotropic fibers in constraining holomorphic extension. Explicit examples, including the orbit $M_{1,1,1} \subset \mathrm{Gr}_3(\mathbb{C}^8)$, illustrate the method and highlight connections with classical constructions in complex geometry and representation theory.
item.dc:creator: Irfan Ullah

item.title: On the $v$-adic values of $G$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2510.11806v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study $G$-functions centered at smooth fibers of one--parameter families of principally polarized abelian varieties. Building on work of Yves Andr\'e, we associate to such families a collection of $G$-functions whose local values admit period interpretations at archimedean places and at finite places of good reduction of the distinguished fiber, and whose radii of convergence control reduction-theoretic proximity at the latter places. We also discuss a conjectural extension to places of bad semistable reduction using Hyodo--Kato cohomology. Specializing to $\mathcal{A}_2$, we construct non-trivial algebraic relations among the values of these $G$-functions at $E^2$- and $E\times\mathrm{CM}$-points in both the archimedean and $p$-adic settings. At non-supersingular finite places of good reduction, we construct relations independent of the place. Finally, we obtain height bounds via Andr\'e-Bombieri's Hasse principle and discuss applications to large Galois orbit estimates and Zilber--Pink finiteness results for curves in $\mathcal{A}_2$.
item.dc:creator: Georgios Papas

item.title: $G$-functions and quaternionic multiplication in $\mathcal{A}_2$
item.description: arXiv:2510.19683v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider $G$-functions associated with one--parameter families of principally polarized abelian surfaces. We construct relations among their values at QM points, under the assumption that the family is Hodge generic and has a distinguished QM point. The proof uses archimedean and $p$-adic period matrices of QM abelian surfaces, via the de Rham--Betti and de Rham--crystalline comparison isomorphisms. As an application of our relations and the Andr\'e--Bombieri Hasse principle, we obtain a height bound for QM points and discuss consequences for the Zilber--Pink conjecture in $\mathcal{A}_2$.
item.dc:creator: Georgios Papas

item.title: Code Equivalence, Point Set Equivalence, and Polynomial Isomorphism
item.description: arXiv:2511.06843v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The linear code equivalence (LCE) problem is known to be equivalent to the point set equivalence (PSE) problem, i.e., the problem to check whether two sets of points in a projective space over a finite field differ by a linear change of coordinates. For such a point set $\mathbb{X}$, let $R$ be its homogeneous coordinate ring and $\mathfrak{J}_{\mathbb{X}}$ its canonical ideal. Then the LCE problem is shown to be equivalent to an algebra isomorphism problem for the doubling $R/\mathfrak{J}_{\mathbb{X}}$. As this doubling is an Artinian Gorenstein algebra, we can use its Macaulay inverse system to reduce the LCE problem to a Polynomial Isomorphism (PI) problem for homogeneous polynomials. The last step is polynomial time under some mild assumptions about the codes. Moreover, for indecomposable iso-dual codes we can reduce the LCE search problem to the PI search problem of degree 3 by noting that the corresponding point sets are self-associated and arithmetically Gorenstein, so that we can use the isomorphism problem for the Artinian reductions of the coordinate rings and form their Macaulay inverse systems.
item.dc:creator: Martin Kreuzer

item.title: Arithmetic volume of Shtukas and Langlands duality
item.description: arXiv:2604.03763v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend the work of Feng--Yun--Zhang relating the arithmetic volume of Shtukas with derivatives of zeta functions by allowing arbitrary coweights for split semisimple algebraic groups. As in their original work, the formula involves some numbers called eigenweights. We obtain uniform formulas for the eigenweights in terms of the Langlands dual group, marking the first structural role for the dual group in such formulas governing derivatives of L-functions.
item.dc:creator: Zeyu Wang, Wenqing Wei

item.title: An infinite series of Gorenstein local algebras failing the affine homogeneity property
item.description: arXiv:2604.04793v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide an infinite series of commutative finite-dimensional Gorenstein local algebras $A_n$ for $n \ge 2$. We give an elementary proof that the maximal ideal of every algebra $A_n$ possesses a one-dimensional subspace that is different from the socle and invariant under the automorphism group of $A_n$. The latter implies that the algebras $A_n$ fail the affine homogeneity property. We also discuss some consequences concerning additive actions on projective hypersurfaces, related to the generalized Hassett-Tschinkel correspondence for these algebras.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Mediterranean Journal of Mathematics, vol. 23 (2026), no. 7, article 224
item.dc:creator: Roman Avdeev, Yulia Zaitseva

item.title: A short proof of a quadratic lower bound on the border determinantal complexity of $x_1^n+\cdots+x_n^n$ over $\mathbb{C}$: A simple human exposition
item.description: arXiv:2606.11090v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: I give a short proof that the border determinantal complexity of $F_n=x_1^n+\cdots+x_n^n$ over $\mathbb{C}$ is at least $(n-1)^2/(4e)$, and at least $(n-1)^2/(2e)$ in the symmetric model. The same argument shows that the border determinantal complexity of $x_1^d+\cdots+x_N^d$ is $\Theta(Nd)$ for all $N\ge3$ and $d\ge2$. The earlier article arXiv:2606.13628, by the same author, introduced the first superlinear lower bounds and includes verification by Lean formalization. However, the AI written exposition was hard to follow. Kumar and Volk (arXiv:2609.34462) give a short proof of the exact ordinary case, but do not address the border or symmetric cases. In this article, I provide a greatly simplified exposition of the border and symmetric cases, using the implicit function theorem and an explicit section of simple solutions in place of the conormal specialization arguments of arXiv:2606.13628. I choose an explicit polynomial system with $n(n-1)^{n-2}$ simple solutions for $F_n$. I then use the implicit function theorem to ensure that each point persists under small perturbations. Finally, kernel equations and the multihomogeneous B\'ezout theorem bound the number of these points for a small determinant. The exposition is due to the human author. The mathematical simplification was obtained in discussion with ChatGPT Astra and refined in conversation with Claude Opus 5.5.
item.dc:creator: Karthik Sheshadri

item.title: Equivariant bordism rigidity for toric manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2609.27412v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we develop a bordism-theoretic approach to rigidity problems for toric and quasitoric manifolds. We prove that two toric manifolds are isomorphic as varieties if and only if they are weakly equivariantly unitary bordant. We also establish a parallel rigidity result for omnioriented quasitoric manifolds satisfying the injectivity condition, showing that their equivariant unitary bordism classes completely determine their omniorientation-preserving equivariant homeomorphism types. Thus, equivariant bordism provides a topological framework for detecting geometric and combinatorial rigidity.
item.dc:creator: Runze Chen, Yuanxin Guan, Zhi L\"{u}

item.title: Cohomology of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families: Newton Polytopes, Weights, and Boundary Monodromy
item.description: arXiv:2610.03081v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, $\psi$ a nontrivial additive character of $\mathbb F_p$, $\psi_q=\psi\circ\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p}$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb F_p^\times$. For $h\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$ let $\Sigma_n(h)$ be the sum of $\psi_q(u_1^{-1}+\cdots+u_n^{-1})$ over $u\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$ with $h_1u_1+\cdots+h_nu_n=-\lambda$, an additively twisted average of products of Kloosterman sums. For every $n\ge2$, the cohomology computing $\Sigma_n(h)$ is concentrated in one degree and has dimension $2^n-1$. It has $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ eigenvalues of weight $n-1$, and its other eigenvalues are the integers $q^{k-1}$, $1\le k\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, with ballot numbers as multiplicities. The part of top weight forms a lisse sheaf $\mathcal W_n$ of rank $r(n)$ on the torus $\mathbb G_m^n$. We determine its local monodromy at the coordinate boundary and its determinant: $\det\mathcal W_n$ is the Artin--Schreier sheaf of the sum $-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(h_1+\cdots+h_n)$ of the critical values of the phase, twisted by $p^{(n+1)r(n)/2}$. The geometric monodromy group of $\mathcal W_n$, and the arithmetic one after normalization to weight $0$, are equal to $\{g\in\mathrm{GL}_{r(n)}:\det(g)^p=1\}$. Consequently the normalized sums become equidistributed like traces of Haar-random elements of $\{g\in\mathrm U(r(n)):\det(g)^p=1\}$. The proofs use Laumon's Fourier transform, middle convolution, the Cayley cubic surface and Larsen's alternative, but no classification of finite groups.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Ebadi

item.title: Moments and Large Geometric Monodromy for Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families
item.description: arXiv:2610.04099v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $q=p^a$ with $p$ prime, $\lambda\in\mathbb F_p^\times$, and $\psi_q=\psi\circ\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p}$ for a nontrivial additive character $\psi$ of $\mathbb F_p$. For $n\ge2$ we study $\Sigma_n(h)=\sum_{u\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n,\sum_i h_i u_i=-\lambda}\psi_q(\sum_i u_i^{-1})$. On $\mathbb G_m^n$ we construct a lisse sheaf $\mathcal W_n$, pure of weight $n+1$ and rank $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, whose Frobenius traces equal $(-1)^{n-1}q\Sigma_n(h)$ minus an explicit polynomial in $q$, for $h\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$. For odd $p$, its geometric monodromy has identity component $\mathrm{SL}_{r(n)}$ and cyclic component group of order divisible by $p$. The full group is $\{g:\det(g)^p=1\}$ for $n=2$, and for $n\ge3$ using boundary unipotence from the companion preprint arXiv:2610.03081. For $p=2$, the sheaf is self-dual and its geometric monodromy is $\mathrm{SO}_{r(n)}$ for odd $n$ and $\mathrm{Sp}_{r(n)}$ for even $n$. After normalization to weight zero, the arithmetic and geometric groups coincide, using the same companion input for odd $p$ and $n\ge3$. As $q\to\infty$ with $p$ fixed, we obtain Sato-Tate laws for centered, normalized sums with error $O(q^{-1/2})$ for polynomial tests and formulas for all power moments. For $p=2$, limiting moments are Gaussian through order $r(n)-1$, with an excess of one above the orthogonal value at order $r(n)$ for odd $n$; if $n+1$ is a power of two, every Frobenius on $\mathcal W_n$ has eigenvalue $q^{(n+1)/2}$. The proof uses $\sum_h|\Sigma_n(h)|^4=c_pq^{3n-2}+O(q^{3n-2-\delta(n)})$ for $n\ge3$, where $c_p=2$ for odd $p$, $c_2=3$ and $\delta(n)=\min(1,(n-2)/2)$, plane sections of the Cayley cubic, exact Frobenius-Schur identities, Laumon's local Fourier transforms and Artin-Schreier theory. For $n=2$ we identify twisted classical Kloosterman sums and compute the fourth moment exactly.

item.title: The Riemann theta function near soliton limit
item.description: arXiv:2610.05716v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It has been known that (the square of) Jacobi elliptic function can be expressed by an infinite sum of single solitons of $\sech^2$ shape. In this paper, we show that there exists a similar structure for higher genus cases. It turns out that this is just a consequence of the quasi-periodicity of the Riemann $\theta$-function. More precisely, we show that the second derivative of $\log \theta$ with the \emph{real} Riemann $\theta$-function of genus $g$ near soliton limit can be well approximated by the \emph{sum} of \emph{real} and \emph{regular} $g$-soliton solutions of Hirota-type in $g$-dimensional real space $\R^g$. This leads to a tessellation of $\R^g$, whose tile is an oblique prism divided into $2^g$ sections by hyper-planes of dominant exponents in the theta function. We apply the results to study quasi-periodic solutions to the KdV and KP equations. We construct the quasi-periodic solutions using the Schottky group, which uniformizes the corresponding Riemann surfaces. We also discuss solitons on quasi-periodic background by pinching some of the homological cycles
